previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with advanced multiple sclerosis and a chronic indwelling Foley catheter, was admitted with weakness and hypotension due to septic shock from a Proteus mirabilis urinary tract infection and bacteremia. He presented with a distended bladder and hydronephrosis due to catheter malposition, which was corrected in the emergency department. He required brief vasopressor support and was treated with intravenous antibiotics, transitioning from piperacillin-tazobactam to ceftriaxone after culture results. A PICC line was placed for outpatient antibiotic therapy. Acute kidney injury improved with supportive care. Complications included a penile erosion from long-term catheter use and recurrent ostomy prolapse, both addressed with surgical and urological follow-up plans. He stabilized over eight days and was discharged home with services for continued IV antibiotics and specialist appointments.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ male with history of multiple sclerosis complicated by 
neurogenic bladder s/p suprapubic catheter placement on 
___ who presents from home with leakage around the 
suprapubic catheter for 4 days.

# Suprapubic catheter leakage: Catheter was exchanged by urology 
in the emergency department. UA revealed >182 WBCs and few 
bacteria so he initially received empiric cefepime and 
vancomycin for a presumed urinary tract infection (he has had 
prior Pseudomonas and E.Coli with ciprofloxacin resistance, and 
also is MRSA positive). However, given that the patient was 
afebrile and asymptomatic, it was ultimately felt that the 
positive urinalysis reflected chronic colonization and 
antibiotics were discontinued. Initial urine cx was consistent 
with fecal contamination; repeat urine culture was pending at 
the time of discharge and will need to be followed up. The 
patient was monitored for 24 hours off antibiotics and remained 
well. He was subsequently discharged home on ___.
